cases.title: Throttle password guessing at the source threshold without locking out the owner

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a password, a one-time-password authenticator and a passkey. Sources src-1, src-2 and src-3 are distinct. The release's declared per-source threshold N, per-account delay schedule and cap, and operator alert threshold for password verification are recorded before running.
steps: Starting from fresh fixture state, submit N minus one wrong passwords for admin-1 from src-1, then the correct password and one-time code.

Starting from fresh fixture state again, submit N wrong passwords from src-1, alternating between the minimal Admin sign-in page and direct calls to the sign-in API, then the correct password and code from src-1 and from src-2.
From src-2 and src-3 in turn, continue wrong passwords for admin-1 until the per-account delay reaches its cap and the alert threshold is crossed, then sign in with admin-1's passkey from src-3.
Have the recovery role run the documented, audited unlock procedure, then sign in from src-3 with the correct password and code.
expectedOutcome: After N minus one failures sign-in still succeeds. After the Nth failure src-1 is blocked by source, so its correct attempt is refused, while src-2 is not blocked; attempts through the minimal Admin and the direct sign-in API count together.
The per-account delay follows the declared schedule and stops at its cap; no number of failures produces indefinite lockout, and passkey sign-in stays available while password attempts are delayed.
Crossing the alert threshold notifies operators once; the unlock is audited and returns password verification to its normal delay.
evidence: Per-attempt source, account, counter, applied delay and outcome; alert, notification and unlock audit records; and the declared threshold values, as evidence for TM-G02-015 and TM-W-059.

cases.title: Expire sessions and recent authentication at their declared edges

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: The fixture deployment reads time through the injectable clock. The declared session idle timeout I, absolute lifetime A and recent-authentication window T are recorded before running.
Each row uses a fresh fixture account that holds rollback permission, a passkey and a one-time-password authenticator.
steps: Leave one session idle for I minus one second and another for I plus one second, then issue an Admin read with each.
Keep a third session active with requests spaced below I until A minus one second and A plus one second after sign-in.
At T minus one second and T plus one second after the last authentication, request enrollment of a second passkey, removal of the one-time-password authenticator and a rollback.
expectedOutcome: Each request inside a limit succeeds; each request past it is refused, and the server-side session record shows the ended state and its reason.
Inside T, enrollment, removal and rollback proceed with their notification and audit records; past T, each requires reauthentication before any change.
evidence: Clock offsets, session records, per-edge request outcomes, reauthentication prompts and notification and audit records, as evidence for TM-G02-016 and TM-W-013.

cases.title: Upgrade password verifiers at the hash-policy edge

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: The release's current password-hash algorithm and cost parameters are recorded. account-1 holds a verifier at that policy, account-2 one at the current algorithm with a cost one step below policy, and account-3 one from a superseded algorithm; each also has a one-time-password authenticator.
steps: Submit one wrong password for each account, then read the stored verifiers and their recorded parameters from PostgreSQL.
Sign each account in with the correct password and code, then read the verifiers again.
Search Admin responses, logs and telemetry for any verifier.
expectedOutcome: Wrong passwords change no verifier.
account-1's verifier is unchanged; account-2's and account-3's verifiers are replaced by current-policy verifiers after their successful sign-in, with the new algorithm and parameters recorded.
No verifier appears in any searched output.
evidence: Verifier algorithm and parameter records before and after, with verifier values reduced to digests, and the search results, as evidence for TM-G02-055.

cases.title: Refuse password-only, alias-host, host-variant and closed bootstrap paths

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a password and a one-time-password authenticator. alias-1 is a verified alias of the single site with an internationalized label, so it has a Unicode form and a punycode form; the deployment declares one proxy. An administrator exists, and the deployment's one-time bootstrap secret was consumed at installation.
steps: Submit admin-1's correct password, skip the second factor, and call an Admin API and an Admin page with the cookies the browser then holds.

Request the Admin sign-in, preview and API namespaces in a browser and with a direct client on alias-1 and on each of its variants: changed letter case, a trailing dot, an explicit port, and its other Unicode or punycode form.
Send the same requests to alias-1 with a forwarded-host value naming the canonical host, from a source that is not the declared proxy.
With a direct client, request the same namespaces on the canonical host with changed letter case, with a trailing dot and with an explicit port.
Call the first-administrator setup path with no secret, with the consumed secret and with a malformed secret.
expectedOutcome: No Admin session or Admin-scoped cookie exists after the password step alone, and both calls are refused as unauthenticated.
Neither alias-1, any of its variants, nor the forwarded-host request answers a reserved namespace or sets a cookie; Admin cookies carry a host prefix and are issued only on the canonical origin.
Each canonical-host variant is either refused or redirected to the exact canonical origin, and no response to a variant sets a cookie.
Each bootstrap attempt receives the same response as an absent route, and the account inventory is unchanged.
evidence: Request and response traces with cookie jars for each row and host variant, and account inventories before and after, as evidence for TM-W-010, TM-W-009 and TM-W-014.

cases.title: Refuse fixed, replayed and revoked session identifiers

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a password, a one-time-password authenticator and a passkey, with session S1 in browser A and S2 in browser B. Browser C holds a session identifier set before sign-in. A separate client keeps a copy of every session cookie.
steps: Sign admin-1 in through browser C as session S3 and compare its identifier with the one set before sign-in.

For each ending event in turn, starting new sessions as needed: sign-out of S1, a password change made from S3, removal of the one-time-password authenticator made from S3, and another administrator's revocation of all admin-1 sessions, present the copied cookie of every session the event should end for an Admin read and a publish call carrying a valid antiforgery token.
expectedOutcome: Browser C receives a new identifier at authentication; the value set before sign-in never becomes authenticated.
Every session an event ends is refused at its next request, for the read as well as the publish call, returns no Admin data and changes nothing; sessions an event does not end continue.
evidence: Server-side session records with versions and end reasons, cookie values recorded only as digests, and per-event request traces, as evidence for TM-G02-016 and TM-W-012.

cases.title: Throttle one-time-code and recovery-code guessing past their declared limits

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a one-time-password authenticator and unused recovery codes, and each run starts from a pending sign-in that has passed the password step; unknown-1 is not an account. Sources src-1, src-2 and src-3 are distinct.

For one-time-code and for recovery-code verification, the release's declared per-source limit, per-account limit, the block or delay each applies at its limit, and the uniform-response latency tolerance E are recorded before running.
steps: From fresh fixture state, submit wrong one-time codes for admin-1 from src-1, alternating between the minimal Admin sign-in page and direct calls to the sign-in API, up to the per-source limit, then one more wrong code and the current correct code from src-1, timing every response.

Continue wrong one-time codes from further sources, each below its per-source limit, until the per-account limit is reached; then, from a source still below its limit, submit the current correct code once before the applied delay elapses and once after it.
Repeat both steps with recovery codes in place of one-time codes, from fresh fixture state.
From src-3, alternate wrong passwords for admin-1 and for unknown-1 an equal number of times, staying below the per-source limit.
expectedOutcome: Attempts through the minimal Admin and through the direct sign-in API count against the same limits, so neither path bypasses them.
At each per-source limit, src-1's next attempt is blocked, and the correct code it then submits is refused without being verified.

At each per-account limit, further attempts from any source are delayed by at least the declared delay. The correct code submitted before the delay elapses is refused, and a refused recovery code is not consumed; the one submitted after the delay succeeds, so the owner is not locked out indefinitely.

Every attempt past a limit is either refused without verification or answered no sooner than the declared delay after the preceding attempt, so no run verifies more codes per window than the declared limits allow.
Unknown-account and wrong-password responses match in status and body, and their median latencies differ by no more than E.
evidence: Per-attempt kind, source, counter, verification flag, applied delay and response time, with the declared limits, delays and tolerance, as evidence for TM-G02-015 and TM-W-059.

cases.title: Reject credential records changed outside enrollment

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 and editor-1 each have an enrolled passkey, and admin-1 also has a one-time-password seed with a known sentinel value. A database fixture can edit account rows directly, and the account tables can be exported without access to the authorized key store.
steps: In PostgreSQL, replace the public key in admin-1's passkey record with editor-1's, then attempt to sign in as admin-1 with editor-1's authenticator.
Restore the record, rebind editor-1's passkey record to admin-1's account identifier, and attempt the same sign-in.
Export the account tables without the key store and examine every seed column.

Search a database dump, logs, telemetry, a backup set after the recovery role decrypts it, and every export the release produces for the sentinel seed in plaintext and in its base32 and hexadecimal encodings.
expectedOutcome: Each altered record fails integrity verification before it is trusted; no session is issued, and the failure is audited.
The export holds only ciphertext seeds tagged with key versions; no seed is readable from the database alone.
The sentinel seed appears in none of the searched outputs in any of those forms.
evidence: Descriptions of each altered row, sign-in refusals, integrity-verification and audit records, the seed-column inspection with values reduced to digests, and the sentinel search results, as evidence for TM-G02-058 and TM-G02-056.

cases.title: Throttle recovery initiation and refuse reused or expired recovery proofs

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a one-time-password authenticator and unused recovery codes, with one consumed code; unknown-1 is not an account. Sources src-1, src-2 and src-3 are distinct, and the outbound message log of the bounded delivery environment is captured.
The release's declared per-source and per-account limits and delays for recovery initiation, and the recovery-token lifetime, are recorded before running.
steps: From fresh fixture state, initiate recovery for admin-1 from src-1 up to its per-source limit and once more, timing every response.
Continue initiation for admin-1 from src-2 and src-3, each below its per-source limit, up to the per-account limit and once more; then initiate once for unknown-1 from src-3.
Present the consumed recovery code, use one issued recovery token twice, and present another token after its declared lifetime.
Submit one unused recovery code in two concurrent attempts from separate clients.
With a fresh token, attempt to complete recovery while removing admin-1's second factor in the same flow, then complete it with the token and a current one-time code.
expectedOutcome: At each limit the next initiation is throttled: no token is issued and no message is sent, and every initiation past a limit is answered no sooner than its declared delay.

Per-source throttling may answer with a throttling status, but per-account throttling returns the same status and body as an accepted initiation, and initiation for unknown-1 matches an accepted one and sends nothing, so no response reveals whether an account exists.
The consumed code, the second use of the token and the expired token are refused.
Exactly one concurrent attempt succeeds and the code is consumed once; the other is refused.
Recovery through the token alone cannot remove the second factor; when recovery completes with the remaining factor, all admin-1 sessions end and the account is notified.
evidence: Per-initiation source, account, counter, applied delay and response time; token issuance and outbound message records; token and code states; and session records and notifications, as evidence for TM-W-011 and TM-G02-057.

cases.title: Require recent authentication for each high-impact Admin operation

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-2 signs in with a password and one-time code and holds the dedicated contact-destination and package-source permissions, import approval and alias administration. Fixture state has a bound repository with a valid dry-run plan, a configured contact destination and verified alias-1.
The injectable clock controls the deployment, and the declared recent-authentication window T is recorded before running. Each row starts from fresh fixture state and a fresh session.
steps: At T minus one second after the last authentication, change the contact destination, rebind the content-package repository, approve and apply the plan, and add alias-2, one operation per row.
At T plus one second after the last authentication, attempt each of the same four operations through the minimal Admin and by direct call, with the permission still held.
In each T-plus-one-second row, reauthenticate in the same session with the one-time code and repeat the operation.
With admin-2's session, request a restore through the minimal Admin and by direct call.
expectedOutcome: Inside the window, each operation succeeds.
At T plus one second, each operation is refused with a reauthentication-required response before any change, through both paths.
After each refusal the destination, repository binding, plan and content, and alias set are unchanged, and no notification is sent.
Each refusal is recorded with actor, operation and the recent-authentication result.
After reauthentication, each operation succeeds once, with its audit record and the notifications it requires.

No Admin or API path performs a restore. W assigns restore to the recovery role outside the minimal Admin, whose separate access AC-031 qualifies; on W, TM-W-013's restore clause therefore applies to no Admin session.
evidence: Clock offsets, per-row and per-path outcomes, state inventories before and after, refusal and success audit records, and notifications, as evidence for TM-W-013.

cases.title: Sign in to the Admin only after a second factor or a passkey

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 has a password and an enrolled one-time-password authenticator; editor-1 has an enrolled passkey. Both accounts are active on the single site. The canonical origin and the declared idle and absolute session lifetimes are recorded.
steps: Through the minimal Admin in a browser, sign in as admin-1 with the password and then the current one-time code.
In a fresh browser profile, sign in as editor-1 with the passkey.
After each sign-in, inspect the issued cookies, the server-side session record and every script-readable browser storage area.
expectedOutcome: Each journey issues one Admin session only after the second factor or passkey assertion completes, with an identifier that differs from any identifier present before authentication.
Session cookies are Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite and host-only with a host prefix, set by the canonical origin; no access or refresh token is in script-readable storage.
Each session has a server-side record with the declared idle and absolute expiry.
evidence: Browser traces of both journeys, cookie identifiers before and after authentication recorded as digests with their attributes, storage inspection results and session records, as evidence for TM-W-010, TM-G02-016, TM-W-009 and TM-W-015.

cases.title: Enroll a passkey and regenerate recovery codes under recent authentication

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: admin-1 signed in with password and one-time code within the declared recent-authentication window and holds an earlier recovery-code set. A second authenticator fixture can create a passkey. The current password-hash policy and seed-encryption key version are recorded.
steps: Enroll the new passkey, then regenerate admin-1's recovery codes and record that the new codes are shown once.
Read admin-1's password verifier, one-time-password seed, recovery-code records and passkey records directly from PostgreSQL.

Sign in once with the new passkey and once with the password and a new recovery code in place of the one-time code, attempt a sign-in with a code from the earlier set, and reload the recovery-code view.
expectedOutcome: Enrollment and regeneration succeed, notify admin-1 and are audited.

The store holds a salted adaptive password verifier with its algorithm and cost, an encrypted seed tagged with its key version, recovery-code verifiers only, and passkey records bound to account, credential and relying-party identifiers with a verifying integrity tag.
Both sign-ins succeed and the new code is consumed once; the earlier-set code is refused, and the view does not show codes again.
evidence: Account-store inspection with secret values reduced to form, length and digest, key-version and hash-parameter records, notifications and audit records, as evidence for TM-W-013, TM-G02-055, TM-G02-056, TM-G02-057 and TM-G02-058.

cases.title: Recover an Admin account after a suspected session compromise

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: Session Sx for editor-1 was established by an attacker fixture with a phished password and one-time code, and its last authentication is older than the recent-authentication window. editor-1 also holds an enrolled passkey and unused recovery codes.
steps: Through Sx, attempt to enroll a new passkey and to remove editor-1's passkey.
As editor-1, start recovery with a recovery code and complete it with the enrolled passkey, then set a new password and regenerate the recovery codes.
Present Sx and the consumed recovery code again, then sign in as editor-1 with the new password and a one-time code.
expectedOutcome: Both factor changes through Sx require reauthentication and change nothing.
Recovery keeps a second factor enrolled throughout, ends every editor-1 session including Sx, notifies the account and invalidates the earlier recovery codes.
Sx and the consumed code are refused; the new sign-in succeeds.
evidence: Session and factor timelines, reauthentication prompts, notifications, audit records and replay refusals, as evidence for TM-W-013, TM-W-011, TM-W-012 and TM-G02-057.

cases.title: Restore and rotate keys without reviving sessions or superseded factors

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: A coordinated backup was taken while admin-1 and editor-1 had active sessions. After it, editor-1 was disabled, admin-1 replaced a passkey and editor-3's rollback permission was removed. The seed-encryption key has a current version and a retained previous version in the authorized store.
steps: Restore the backup into an isolated recovery deployment and present both sessions' cookies from the backup point.

As the recovery role, review the presented account, factor and permission changes made after the backup point; reapply editor-1's disablement and the removal of editor-3's rollback permission, remove admin-1's superseded passkey and have admin-1 enroll the replacement again.

Sign in as admin-1 with password and one-time code and with the replacement passkey; attempt editor-1's sign-in and a sign-in with the superseded passkey; and have editor-3 sign in and attempt a rollback.
Rotate the seed-encryption key, sign in with a one-time code, then restore the rotated state again and repeat.
expectedOutcome: Every restored session is refused and fresh sign-in is required; the review lists all three post-backup changes, including the permission removal.
After reapplication, editor-1, the superseded passkey and editor-3's rollback are refused, and admin-1's current factors work.
Seeds decrypt only through the authorized key store, across rotation and the second restore.
evidence: Restore identities, session refusals, the post-backup change review, reapplication audit records, key versions and sign-in outcomes, as evidence for TM-W-049 and TM-G02-056.

cases.title: Recover an interrupted first-administrator setup

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: A clean W deployment has no administrator and holds a one-time bootstrap secret issued to it. Setup can be interrupted after the secret is presented and before the account commits.
steps: Interrupt setup at that point, restart the container, and inspect the account store and the secret's recorded state.
Complete setup with the secret, enrolling a second factor, then present the same secret from a second client and call the setup path again.
expectedOutcome: The interruption leaves no partial administrator; the secret is either still usable once or consumed together with a committed account, never both.
After completion the setup path is unreachable and the secret is refused; the new administrator receives an Admin session only after a second factor or passkey.
evidence: Fault-point traces, account and secret states before and after restart, refused reuse traces and audit records, as evidence for TM-W-014 and TM-W-010.

cases.title: Remove an attacker-enrolled passkey through the owner's recovery

scope.website: W minimal Admin sign-in with a password plus a second factor or a passkey, account recovery, session revocation, stored credential forms, guessing and lockout resistance, and first-administrator bootstrap on the canonical origin. Registration, external login, passwordless links and shared-account tenant membership are outside W.

preconditions: An attacker fixture holds session Sy for editor-2, established with a phished password and one-time code and still inside the recent-authentication window. editor-2 holds an enrolled one-time-password authenticator and unused recovery codes, and editor-2's messages in the bounded delivery environment are captured.
steps: Through Sy, change editor-2's password and enroll an attacker passkey, then sign in with that passkey as session Sz from a second attacker client.
As editor-2, start recovery with a recovery code and complete it with the one-time-password authenticator.
During recovery, review the enrolled factors, remove the attacker passkey, set a new password and regenerate the recovery codes.
Present Sy and Sz again, and attempt a sign-in with the removed passkey.
expectedOutcome: Both changes inside the window succeed, are audited and notify editor-2 immediately; editor-2's own sessions end with the password change.
Completed recovery ends Sy, Sz and every other editor-2 session and notifies the account; the passkey removal is audited, and the removed record no longer verifies.
Sy, Sz and the removed passkey are refused afterward, while editor-2's one-time-password authenticator, new password and new recovery codes work.
evidence: Factor enrollment and removal timeline, notifications with their delivery times, session records with end reasons, audit records, and refused replay and sign-in traces, as evidence for TM-W-013, TM-W-011, TM-W-012 and TM-G02-058.

cases.title: Measure permission revocation at the declared freshness bound

scope.reference: G-02 server-authoritative permissions, resource grants, settings, features, delegation and claim and session freshness through direct API, advertised client, integration and background entry points on shared-database tenancy. Canonical Admin UI qualification is G-03 work; sign-in fixtures come from AC-002.

preconditions: In tenant-A, user-1 holds item.read and item.export with warm authorization cache entries. The release's declared freshness bound B for cached authorization and its classification of item.export as security-sensitive are recorded before running.
steps: Revoke item.read and record the instant the change is authoritative.
Read item-1 through the direct API and the advertised .NET and TypeScript clients at B minus one second and B plus one second after that instant.
Start an export, revoke item.export while it runs, and request its result; repeat with user-1's session revoked instead.

cases.title: Rotate secrets and keys at their declared lifecycle edges

scope.website: W ASVS Level 2 applicability and production posture for the public, Admin, API, preview, import and contact surfaces: content security policy and framing on the shared origin, HTTPS, release and dependency provenance against the dependency register, secret, key and telemetry handling, hostile package and source input, media scanning and quarantine, host validation and canonical links, contact antispam, public rate limits, backups, and container and network limits. preconditions: The email transport credential, the data-protection key ring and the one-time-password seed key each have a current version and a documented rotation procedure. steps: Rotate the transport credential and send contact mail immediately before and after the previous credential is revoked.
Point the transport at an endpoint that presents an unverifiable certificate and send contact mail.
Rotate the key ring and present the earlier session cookie before and after the previous key's declared end.
Rotate the seed key and verify a one-time code for an account whose seed was encrypted under the previous key.
expectedOutcome: Delivery succeeds under each valid credential and is a recorded delivery failure under the revoked one; the unverifiable certificate is a delivery failure with no unencrypted fallback.
The earlier cookie is accepted until the previous key's declared end and refused after it.
The earlier seed still verifies through the authorized key store after rotation.

scope.website: W ASVS Level 2 applicability and production posture for the public, Admin, API, preview, import and contact surfaces: content security policy and framing on the shared origin, HTTPS, release and dependency provenance against the dependency register, secret, key and telemetry handling, hostile package and source input, media scanning and quarantine, host validation and canonical links, contact antispam, public rate limits, backups, and container and network limits. preconditions: Sentinel values are mounted as the database password, transport credential and Git source credential through deployment secret references. An anonymous probe and an operator holding diagnostics permission are available.
steps: Inspect every image layer and the image configuration for the sentinels.
Request liveness, readiness and diagnostics as the anonymous probe and as the operator, with the database available and unavailable, and export a diagnostic bundle as the operator.
Cause a database outage and a transport failure, then search logs, traces, metrics and the bundle for sentinels, session cookies and contact bodies, and inspect metric dimensions.

preconditions: The contact form has a configured named destination. Sources src-1 to src-4 are distinct, and the bounded delivery environment captures outbound messages.
steps: From src-1, submit one request failing each check that the declared antispam policy lists, and one that replays an antispam response already accepted for another submission.
From src-2, submit valid requests up to the per-source limit and once more; from src-3, continue toward the same destination until the per-destination limit is reached and once more.
Submit a request whose fields exceed the declared size bounds; after the windows elapse, submit from many sources the largest burst of valid requests that the submission limits allow.
After the windows elapse again, submit one valid request from src-4.
expectedOutcome: Each antispam failure, including the replayed response, is refused with a stable code; nothing is stored as an accepted request and no mail is queued.
At each submission limit the next request is refused, and no request past a limit is accepted or queued.
The oversized request is refused before processing. The burst is accepted and queued, and outbound mail never exceeds the delivery cap per window.
src-4's request is accepted and delivered once.
evidence: Per-request source, antispam results, limit counters and dispositions; accepted-request and outbound queue inventories; and the delivery rate per window, as evidence for TM-W-030.

Request public pages, error pages, media, health, Admin and preview responses over HTTPS and once over plain HTTP, and inspect their headers.
